headline: Cash NPAT (continuing operations) rose $730m or 7.1%, from $10,252m in FY25 to $10,982m in FY26. Statutory NPAT rose $778m ($10,133m to $10,911m) - $48m more than cash - as non-cash drags eased (transaction costs/disposals -$172m to -$17m; hedging/IFRS volatility +$53m to -$54m). Quantified cash drivers are drags: underlying operating expenses +$719m (6%; IT +$393m, staff +$288m) and +$40m more expense notable items; cash ETR fell 50bps to 30.0% (unquantified tailwind). NII, other operating income and impairment are unquantified in evidence, leaving a +$1,489m residual; the 30bps efficiency-ratio gain implies income outgrew expenses.

drivers.narrative: Underlying operating expenses (cash basis) rose $719m or 6% to $13,585m (FY25: $12,866m): IT services +$393m (16%), staff +$288m (4%), other expenses +$57m (4%), partly offset by occupancy and equipment -$19m (2%). This is the underlying figure; notable items are stated separately.

Non-underlying expense items (total operating expenses less underlying) rose from $130m in FY25 to $170m in FY26 - a $40m incremental drag on cash NPAT - treated as notable/restructuring items per bank labelling; composition not detailed in provided evidence.

Cash effective tax rate fell 50bps from 30.5% to 30.0%, primarily due to lower non-deductible expenses - a positive driver. Dollar contribution is not derivable (pre-tax cash profit not provided in evidence) and is subsumed in the residual.

Net interest income movement is not quantified in the provided records - no volume/margin dollar bridge. The underlying expense-to-income ratio fell 30bps to 44.9%, implying underlying operating income grew faster than the 6% expense growth, but the NII share is not evidenced.

Fees, trading, insurance and other income movement is not quantified in the provided records; only aggregate underlying income growth is implied by the efficiency-ratio improvement. Contribution subsumed in the residual.
Loan impairment expense movement is not quantified or described in the provided evidence records; direction and magnitude unknown, subsumed in the residual.

notable_items: Cash NPAT excludes non-cash items: transaction costs and gains/(losses) on disposals (-$17m FY26 vs -$172m FY25) and hedging/IFRS volatility (-$54m FY26 vs +$53m FY25) - ev-15, ev-16.
Expense notable items (total less underlying operating expenses): $170m FY26 vs $130m FY25, computed from ev-10 and ev-11.
Statutory NPAT of $10,911m described as 'broadly in line' with cash NPAT of $10,982m - ev-13, ev-14.

Its two captured bars equal the year-on-year change in non-cash items and are used only to reconcile statutory vs cash movements.

disagreements.topic: FY26 vs FY25 NPAT movement: cash vs statutory
disagreements.explanation: Cash basis excludes non-cash items; the year-on-year change in those items (+$155m smaller transaction/disposal cost drag, -$107m hedging swing = +$48m) makes statutory growth exceed cash growth by $48m.

limitations: No period-matching NPAT walk exists in the evidence: the only walk (ev-1, presentation p23) fails its sum check (10,133 + 48 = 10,181 vs 10,982) and mixes a statutory FY25 start with a cash FY26 endpoint, so its bars are used only for the statutory-vs-cash reconciliation, never as FY26-vs-FY25 cash attribution.

Net interest income, other operating income and loan impairment expense movements are not quantified in the provided records; the +$1,489m residual comprises these lines plus the unquantified tax benefit. The cash income statement (NII, other operating income, LIE, tax expense, FY26 vs FY25) or a profit-announcement NPAT walk would be required to complete the bridge.
Tax contribution is directional only: the 50bps cash ETR decline is evidenced, but pre-tax cash profit is not provided, so the dollar benefit cannot be computed.
Expense notable items ($170m FY26 vs $130m FY25) are computed as total less underlying operating expenses (ev-10, ev-11); their composition is not disclosed in the evidence.

Expense and tax evidence comes solely from the profit announcement; the presentation corroborates only NPAT levels and the statutory-cash reconciliation, so single-document driver claims are capped at 85 confidence.

The efficiency ratio improvement (45.2% to 44.9%, ev-9) implies underlying operating income grew faster than the 6% expense growth, but the NII vs other-income split is unavailable; no dollar figure is inferred from rounded ratios.
